rules: A feature is verified only when every acceptance criterion has evidence: a command that passed, with its output recorded in verification.evidence.
Acceptance criteria are never removed or weakened to reach verified. Changing one needs a decision entry in harness/decisions.md.
Mocked engine responses never count as evidence for a criterion that names the real engine.

features.title: Persistent engineering harness
features.description: Repository-held engineering context: instructions, product and architecture documents, feature registry, progress, decisions, blockers, agent roles, the engineering-loop skill, hooks, verify and loop scripts.
acceptance: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, PRODUCT.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, README.md exist and state invariants, boundaries and session start/end steps.
harness/features.json validates against scripts/check_features.py (ids unique, dependencies exist, statuses allowed, verified features carry evidence).
harness/progress.md, decisions.md, blockers.md exist and are current.
scripts/verify.sh runs the registry check and every implemented gate and exits non-zero on failure.
scripts/loop.sh is opt-in, bounded (iterations, minutes, no-progress stop) and never uses permission bypass.
.claude/ holds project-local settings with reviewed hooks, five agent roles and the engineering-loop skill.
docs/open-source-integration-registry.md records every considered project with license and decision.

features.title: Audit and verify existing OpenMHS capabilities
features.description: Establish from source and real runs which OpenMHS capabilities the platform can rely on, at a pinned commit.
acceptance: docs/openmhs-capability-audit.md lists each claimed capability with status (verified by run, present in source, not found) and the evidence.
The 469-record / 124-verdict fixture is confirmed by count.
At least one real ops ingest + ops compare --json and one outcome verify --json run is recorded with output.
Interface gaps are recorded in docs/engine-contract-gaps.md without modifying OpenMHS.

evidence: python scripts/audit_openmhs.py (pinned release binary sha256:d51af06f..., commit e9ef873): 11/11 checks passed; output in harness/evaluation-results/openmhs-audit.json
coresense_real_flights_verified.jsonl: 469 records, 124 outcome.verified (counted by the audit)
ops ingest + ops compare --json (gazebo A/B, reported and verified), ops incidents/show --json, ops compare --paired, outcome verify --json on 27/27 corpus cases recorded in the audit output
docs/openmhs-capability-audit.md and docs/engine-contract-gaps.md (G-1..G-6) written; OpenMHS clone unmodified (git status clean in D:/openmhs-di)

limitations: Upstream Rust test suite not re-run here (RAM/disk); the audit exercises the CLI surface the platform uses.
Gateway, MCP and Python importers are present in source but not exercised (not used by the platform).

features.title: Version-pinned OpenMHS bridge
features.description: Python package that runs the pinned OpenMHS binary without a shell, validates its JSON output, and records engine provenance.
acceptance: scripts/build-openmhs.sh builds the binary from the commit in engine.lock.json without modifying the OpenMHS clone, and records its SHA-256.
The bridge refuses a binary whose SHA-256 differs from the configured one.
Every invocation uses an argument list (no shell), a timeout, and a bounded output size; untrusted strings never reach a shell.
ops ingest / compare / incidents / show and outcome verify outputs are parsed into typed models; an unexpected shape is a structured error, not a crash.

Integration tests run the real binary on the pinned fixtures and reproduce the Gazebo A/B comparison (verified: a 15/30 attempts failed, b 0/30, Newcombe difference -0.5) and the 124 verdicts fixture.
Engine version, binary SHA-256, commit and rules version are attached to every result.

evidence: OPENMHS_SRC_REPO=C:/Users/HP/Open-MHS CARGO_OFFLINE=1 scripts/build-openmhs.sh --jobs 2: release build in 9m20s from git archive of e9ef873; .engine/build.json sha256:d51af06ff90e01b8a672f468712657f4c248db7a633529c9724957e0ae602e41

PAP_REQUIRE_ENGINE=1 uv run pytest packages/openmhs-bridge: 31 passed (digest mismatch refused, no-shell argv, NUL refused, timeout/cancel/output cap kill the process, invalid output -> engine.output_invalid, gazebo A/B reproduced 15/30 -> 0/30 newcombe -0.5, 469/124 fixture ingested with 9 incidents, paired McNemar p=0.5078, Python manifest digests == engine digests, hostile release labels stay values, unexpected manifest resolution -> engine.input_rejected, conditions_of parity with OpenMHS original)
uv run mypy packages/openmhs-bridge/src (strict): no issues; uv run ruff check: clean

limitations: Engine digest is per platform; Linux digest for the Compose image will be recorded when INF-003 builds it.
An unknown release label is answered by the engine with an empty arm and a warning (exit 0); callers must pass expect_a/expect_b, which the pipeline will do.

features.title: Versioned evidence and episode contracts
features.description: Versioned schemas for mapping configurations, normalized episodes and evaluation reports, published as JSON Schema and TypeScript.
acceptance: Pydantic models are the single source; JSON Schemas are generated into packages/contracts/schema and checked for drift in verify.sh.

Every normalized episode carries organization, project, robot, site, task, scenario, release, timestamps, source artifact + locator, mapping revision and evaluation configuration, or an explicit unavailable marker for each optional one.
Schema version is carried in every persisted document.

features.title: Commercial application scaffold
features.description: FastAPI service with PostgreSQL, SQLAlchemy, Alembic, health checks; Next.js web application.
acceptance: API starts against PostgreSQL; /healthz reports database and engine status.
Alembic upgrade head then downgrade base then upgrade head succeeds on an empty PostgreSQL database.
ruff, mypy (strict for app/) and pytest pass.
Web app builds with next build, strict TypeScript, ESLint and Vitest passing.

features.title: Organization and project authorization boundaries
features.description: OIDC bearer-token authentication, organization membership with admin/engineer/viewer roles, project-scoped resource checks, service credentials, audited decisions.
acceptance: OIDC access tokens are validated (signature against JWKS, issuer, audience, expiry); tests use a locally generated key set, not a bypass.
A development identity mode exists only when PAP_AUTH_MODE=dev and is refused when PAP_ENV=production.
Every project-scoped route resolves the project through the caller's organization; a resource id from another organization returns 404, never data.
Viewer cannot write; engineer cannot manage members; admin can.
Service credentials are stored hashed, scoped to one organization and role, and revocable.
Each allow/deny on a protected write is recorded as an audit event.
A parametrized test calls every protected route as an outsider and asserts no cross-organization data is returned.

features.title: Register baseline and candidate releases
features.description: Releases (software or policy) with an OpenMHS deployment manifest whose canonical digest matches the engine's.
acceptance: POST/GET releases per project; label unique per project; manifest stored with its canonical SHA-256.
The Python canonical digest equals the digest the engine reports for the same manifest (integration test with the real binary).
A policy release must carry an immutable model revision (digest or commit), otherwise it is refused.

features.title: Validated evidence upload and storage
features.description: Upload of source evidence into content-addressed, immutable storage with size limits and safe parsing.
acceptance: Uploads are streamed with a configurable byte limit; over-limit uploads are refused with 413 and leave nothing stored.
Stored objects are addressed by SHA-256; re-uploading identical bytes returns the existing artifact; stored bytes are never overwritten.
Filenames are never used as storage paths; path traversal attempts are refused or neutralised and tested.
Only declared media types are accepted (CSV, JSONL, JSON); archives are refused until archive extraction protection exists.
A local filesystem adapter and an S3-compatible adapter implement one storage interface; the S3 adapter is tested against a real S3-compatible server or marked unverified.

features.title: Declarative episode mapping
features.description: Versioned mapping revisions that turn CSV/JSONL rows into episodes, RFC 0005 events and RFC 0004 evidence records, with a validation report.
acceptance: Mapping revisions are immutable; editing creates a new version with its own SHA-256.

The mapping declares input format, timestamp interpretation, episode key, robot, site, task, scenario, reported outcome, independent measurements with units, the outcome contract and a missing-data policy.
A validation report lists every row that was rejected or had a field marked unavailable, with row number and reason; no row disappears silently (rows in = episodes + rejected rows).
Missing metadata is marked unavailable, never invented; a required field that is missing rejects the row.
Produced events are accepted by the real engine's ops ingest with zero rejections on the demo dataset.

features.title: Durable evaluation jobs
features.description: PostgreSQL-backed jobs with queued/running/succeeded/failed/cancelled states, run by a separate worker process.
acceptance: Submitting the same inputs twice returns the same job (idempotency by input checksum).
The worker claims jobs with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and a lease; two workers never run one job.
A job whose worker died (lease expired) is re-queued on recovery and finishes; tested by killing a worker process.
Timeouts, bounded retries for transient errors, structured errors, and cancellation of queued and running jobs are tested.
Evaluation never runs inside an HTTP request handler.

features.title: Execute a real OpenMHS release comparison
features.description: The worker verifies outcomes with openmhs outcome verify, ingests events with ops ingest and compares releases with ops compare, reported and verified.
acceptance: A job over the demo dataset runs the real binary for verification, ingest and both comparisons.
Ingest rejections or manifest digests the engine does not resolve fail the job with a structured error.
Results equal a direct CLI run on the same events file (byte-identical compare JSON).

features.title: Persist evaluation results and provenance
features.description: Comparison outputs, per-episode verdicts and the evidence bundle (events file, engine store, verifier reports) persisted with checksums.
acceptance: Each result row records engine version, binary SHA-256, commit, rules version, mapping revision, input artifact checksums and the evaluation configuration.
The events file and engine store are stored as immutable artifacts; re-running the engine on the stored events file reproduces the stored comparison.

features.title: Release Intelligence API
features.description: Documented REST endpoints for comparisons, episodes and evidence, published as OpenAPI with a generated TypeScript client.
acceptance: OpenAPI document is generated and committed; the TypeScript client is generated from it and checked for drift.
Comparison endpoint returns the engine's comparison unchanged plus provenance; no statistic is computed in the API.
Episode list supports filtering by release, outcome class, scenario, site and robot with pagination.

features.title: Functional Release Intelligence interface
features.description: Web workflow: select project, releases and evidence, run an evaluation, read the comparison with uncertainty and warnings.
acceptance: Every number on the comparison page comes from the API; tests assert no hard-coded metrics.
Reported and verified outcomes are shown separately with sample counts, confidence intervals, unknown rate and the engine's verdict and reasons.
insufficient_evidence and warnings are shown prominently, not hidden.
Loading, empty and failure states are covered by Vitest; the full flow by Playwright against the real API and engine.

features.title: Episode-level evidence inspection
features.description: Drill down from a comparison to episodes, their verdict reasons, measurements, units and the source rows.
acceptance: Episode detail shows reported outcome, verdict, verifier reasons, each condition with observed values and units, source artifact and row, mapping revision and engine metadata.
Contradictory and unknown outcomes explain why, from the verifier report.

features.title: Reproducible HTML and JSON reports
features.description: Export of a comparison as a self-contained HTML report and a machine-readable JSON report.
acceptance: The JSON report embeds input checksums, engine provenance, mapping revision and the engine outputs; generating it twice gives identical bytes.
The HTML report is rendered from the JSON report only and states the evidence class (synthetic, simulated, production).

features.title: Tenant isolation and upload security
features.description: Cross-tenant, upload, parsing and container hardening checks.
acceptance: Isolation test covers every route registered in the application (route list introspected, not hand-written).
Malformed CSV/JSONL, oversized rows, deeply nested JSON and non-UTF-8 input produce validation errors, not crashes.
Containers run as non-root; the worker has CPU, memory and time limits.
gitleaks, Trivy and Semgrep run in CI.

features.title: Reproducible Docker Compose environment
features.description: docker compose up starts PostgreSQL, object storage, API, worker (with the pinned engine) and web.
acceptance: One documented command starts all services; health checks pass.
The engine is built from engine.lock.json inside the image build, not copied from a developer machine.
Verified on a clean machine or CI runner.

features.title: Real OpenMHS-backed demonstration
features.description: Labelled synthetic warehouse pick-and-place dataset taken through the whole workflow end to end.
acceptance: The dataset is generated by a seeded script, labelled synthetic in every file and report, and contains successes, missed grasps, drops, operator interventions, contradictions, unknowns and several scenarios for a baseline and a candidate.
Playwright drives create project -> releases -> upload -> evaluate -> compare -> episode drilldown -> export against the real API, worker and engine.
Worker restart recovery, duplicate submission, invalid artifact, unauthorized access, incompatible comparison and insufficient samples are exercised.

features.title: Operational observability
features.description: Structured logs, OpenTelemetry traces over OTLP, Prometheus metrics for API and worker.
acceptance: Logs are JSON with request and job ids and never contain tokens or uploaded content.
Job duration, state counts and engine failures are exported as metrics.
Traces span API request -> job -> engine invocation.
